title: Is Dropshipping Worth It in 2026? - Shopify
summary: Platform article: dropshipping still viable with caveats on thin margins, competition, marketing cost, supplier reliability, and a year or more to replace an income.

assertions.quote: Sales don’t start coming in just because your store has gone live.
dropshippers don’t have to buy any inventory upfront
Dropshipping margins are often thinner than they look at first glance.
low barrier to entry for you means low barrier to entry for your competitors

verdicts.note: Same catalog and same suppliers, so price and ad competition is structural.

assertions.quote: it takes at least a year of full-time work to recreate the average full-time income through dropshipping

verdicts.note: Plausible for those who succeed, but there is no independent data and most stores never get there.

assertions.quote: Only 34.7% of all US private-sector business establishments started in March 2013 were still operating a decade later.

verdicts.note: BLS establishment survival data show roughly half gone by year five; low-cost online stores likely churn faster.

assertions.quote: those younger purchasers understand that they can just buy those products for a cheaper price on sites like Temu and Alibaba

verdicts.note: Reverse image search and direct-from-China marketplaces have compressed resale margins on generic goods.

assertions.quote: The only way to be successful in dropshipping nowadays is to have a real identity as a brand

verdicts.note: Branding helps differentiate identical goods, but it is not sufficient and some generic stores still profit short-term.

assertions.quote: incorporating AI tools into dropshipping processes can drastically cut down time on things like product research and trend detection
